name: degen_t08
hypothesis: The 55.8% degenerate-repetition rate of SFT v2 (vs base 0-shot 24.7%, base 3-shot 6.6%) is produced by greedy decoding, not by the model. READ: degeneracy at t=0.8 below base's 24.7% => the loop is a decoding artifact and every greedy code-500 number today is measuring the decoder; at or above 55.8% => the model itself is non-terminating and the cause is upstream in the SFT data or recipe. Accuracy at t=0.8 is a different estimator than greedy and is NOT comparable to the 2.2%.
finding: The repetition loop is a greedy-decoding artifact: sampling at t=0.8 cuts degeneracy by two thirds, below base 0-shot's 25.4%. It hid nothing -- accuracy stayed on the floor and in fact fell (greedy is the better pass@1 estimator for a weak model). So the format-side numbers (fence rate, degeneracy) are properties of the decoder and must be reported with their temperature; the capability-side number (accuracy at the floor) is decoder-independent and now rests on firmer ground, having been suspected of being a decoder artifact and checked.
decision: Report every generative format metric with its temperature; do not build a repetition penalty (it would suppress a symptom that carries no capability signal); do not change the SFT recipe or the SFT pack on this evidence. The 200M-has-no-measurable-code-generation conclusion stands.

name: degen_t08_base
hypothesis: Control arm for degen_t08, missing from the original design: base 0-shot code-500 was scored greedy (0/497, degeneracy 25.4%). If greedy also suppresses base accuracy, the 'no measurable code generation at 200M' conclusion rests partly on a decoder artifact. READ: base t=0.8 accuracy still 0/497 (or below 12.6%) => the capability conclusion is decoder-independent and stands. Above 12.6% => every base code number today measured the decoder and the conclusion is void.
finding: The control arm the original design was missing. Sampling halves degeneracy on the base model too and moves accuracy not at all -- it was already exactly zero and stays exactly zero. So the capability conclusion is decoder-independent: across two checkpoints and two temperatures, every code accuracy sits on the floor while the degeneracy rate moves by 13-39 points. Degeneracy and accuracy are separate channels and only the first responds to the decoder.
decision: '200M has no measurable code generation in this regime' is confirmed and no longer needs the decoder caveat. Report generative FORMAT metrics with their temperature; capability metrics do not need it.

name: ab_untie_head
hypothesis: 1e 的问题：b0-10 的 embedding 放大是否来自 head 以 lr 0.1 训练。
result: ANSWERED WITHOUT A CARD, so the A/B is cancelled rather than queued.
finding: tied tok.weight already contains three row classes that each eat exactly one gradient path: [0,32773) input+head, [32773,32784) HEAD ONLY (in head.weight[:vocab], never an input id, never a target), [32784,32832) neither. step2500->3000: head-only rows 13.2399 -> 13.8540 = 1.0464x, input+head median 76.6132 -> 90.2697 = 1.1783x, no-path rows max abs delta exactly 0 (so the read has no noise floor). The head path DOES amplify -- 1e's direction is right -- but it is ln1.0464/ln1.1783 = 27.6% of the growth; 72.4% is the input path. The 11 head-only rows are bit-identical to each other, so that path's gradient is a term SHARED by all rows (the softmax denominator), which is also the mechanism behind 4.6's 'same multiple at every quantile'.
decision: Do not run it. Untie is also NOT parameter-matched: our head is tied (model.py:322), so untying adds 33.6M params = +17% at 200M, moving capacity and lr together -- an honest test needs three arms (tied / untied-same-lr / untied-low-lr), 3x the cost, to answer a question the free read already answered. If anyone runs it anyway, the reading is 'do head-only rows stop growing', NOT total norm, which will only fall by under a third and read as 'no effect'.

hypothesis: A/B (2a) speedrun record: Muon lr x max(1, out/in)^0.5 per parameter shape. Muon orthogonalises its update, so every column of X carries roughly unit RMS whatever the shape -- a tall (fan-out) matrix therefore takes a per-element step that is small relative to its weight, and the factor restores it. MEASURED AFFECTED SET on this exact config (d=1024, L=12, heads=8, ffn_hidden=3072): 36 of 63 Muon tensors, factors kv_up [2048,256] 2.8284, w13 [6144,1024] 2.4495, qkv [3072,1024] 1.7321, qg [2048,1024] 1.4142, gb [1040,1024] 1.0078; o, w2 and kv_down get exactly 1.0 from the clamp. PREDICTION: kv_up carries the largest factor of anything in the model (MLA latent is d/4, so it is the tallest by ratio) and is where an instability would appear first -- watch its weight norm, not just the loss. This arm is 2a ONLY: NorMuon (beta2 0.9) and the momentum-to-0.85 tail are a SECOND arm, deliberately not bundled, because three changes in one arm cannot say which one moved the loss. That asymmetry is enough for the recipe decision (a change with no upside and a consistent downside sign does not go in) and NOT enough for a quantitative claim about the cost. The arm really was the arm. gnorm tells the story: 54.85 at step 10 against baseline 1.71, i.e. the identity start makes the first real update violent rather than gentle, and by step 300 gnorm is still 1.44 vs 0.87. What zero-init bought was a delayed and rougher start, not a smoother one.
decision: zero_init_out does NOT enter the recipe (1e concurs, 2026-09-02 18:0xZ). Flag stays in train.py/model.py, default False, guarded by scripts/test_zero_init_out.py -- it costs nothing off and re-running it at another scale is one flag. The identical overall is therefore real and uninformative -- with n=277 and 5 dimensions the accuracy is a ratio of small integers, and equal totals from unequal parts is an ordinary outcome, not a signal.

SAME BORROWED-SIGMA CAVEAT AS (3), and here it cuts the other way, which is the point worth keeping: the 0.24 bar comes from ds.seed_variance_0p2b, four 0.2b runs (world 7, mix_scale_0.2b, warmup 20, fp8 True). The bar is 4.65 sigma, so -0.0611 would clear it once sigma < 0.0131 -- sigma would have to fall to a QUARTER of the measured 0.0516, which is a bigger stretch than (3)'s halving. decision: muon_shape_lr is a CANDIDATE, not adopted and not rejected -- the opposite disposition from zero_init_out, on the same magnitude of evidence, because the sign is reversed and the cost is nil. name: ab_value_embed
cmd: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,4,5,6,7 ARM=valueembed STEPS=500 scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh  # readout: scripts/eval_all.py on card 5; rows in runs/score_matrix.jsonl; row-norms: python3 scripts/ve_row_norms.py --ckpt ckpt_ab_valueembed_valueembed.pt.ep1 --out runs/ve_row_norms.json
notes: logs runs/ab_valueembed_valueembed.log (arm), runs/ab_shapelr_base.log (base, reused from A/B 2a), runs/ab_ve_readout.log (both readouts).
result: FLAT on both pre-registered readings. domain_loss unweighted_mean base 2.8480 -> VE 2.8479, delta -0.0001 nat against a 0.24 nat bar (0.04% of it); minimal_pairs base 0.7148 -> VE 0.7040, -1.08pt against an 11.5pt bar (9.4% of it, and in the WRONG direction). val loss 2.603 -> 2.598 (-0.005, 2% of the bar), train 2.332 -> 2.324. Per-domain the sign is split 6 of 9 to VE and every domain moves less than 0.02: math_owm -0.0060, cot -0.0050, textbook -0.0061, zh_web -0.0016, code_starcoder -0.0112, code_rp1t -0.0064 for VE; en_c4 +0.0037, chat_qa +0.0112, chatml +0.0200 against. Both arms world 4, same 500 steps, 0.26B tokens, seed 42, mix_200m_4b, and the arm's cfg-diff line reads exactly: `cfg non-default: accum=2, anneal_frac=0.0, batch=16, mix='data/mix_200m_4b.json', value_embed=True, warmdown=0.1, warmup=300` -- value_embed is the only mechanism field, so arm identity is in the log rather than inferred from the checkpoint. Base is ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt.ep1, REUSED from A/B (2a); unlike the (3)/(2a) pair it is world 4 like this arm, so tokens/step match and the same step is the same token position. Two differences are by design and neither is a defect: the parameter difference (+33,659,904, +16.3%) IS the intervention, and the tree difference between the two runs is outside the training path. Throughput: both arms hold 57K tok/s/gpu at steady state, so the +16.3% parameters cost no measured tokens/s here -- stated as tok/s and param count only, NOT as free compute: reported MFU rises 48% -> 55% purely because mfu = 6*n_params*tps/peak (train.py:2560) puts n_params in the numerator while 99.9% of the added params are a gather with no matmul. Wall 1321s -> 1250s.
finding:
THE TABLE IS FULLY TRAINED, WHICH KILLS THE PRE-REGISTERED WATCH RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. The row-norm reading (scripts/ve_row_norms.py, runs/ve_row_norms.json) reads 32832 of 32832 rows above the decay floor -- not a few frequent rows. The WATCH text assumed 'a small fraction' of rows get touched at 500 steps; that was wrong by construction: 0.26B tokens over 32832 rows is ~7900 hits per row on average. So the 'few frequent rows won' branch was never live, and with the A/B flat there is no win to attribute either way. Movement is also NOT concentrated: the top 1000 rows of 32832 hold 15.9% of total delta, top 100 hold 2.7%, top 10 hold 0.3%.
THE FLOOR HAD TO BE MEASURED, AND THE ESTIMATED ONE INVERTED THE ANSWER. Three premises died before this number was usable, all of them caught: (a) 'rows differing from init were trained' reads the whole vocab, because the table sits in the AdamW `embed` group (train.py:779) and an Embedding's gradient is DENSE, so decoupled decay steps every row whether a token reached it or not; (b) 'a norm cutoff separates them' fails too -- the model inits embeddings to std=0.02 (model.py:453 via self.apply(self._init) at :388), so an untouched row keeps norm 0.02*sqrt(1024) = 0.64, and I had earlier quoted 32 from torch's N(0,1) default, which is not this model's init; (c) the floor I first used was ESTIMATED at 10x the median row on the premise that most rows stay untouched, and that premise is the very thing being tested -- it put the floor ~900x too high and reported 274 of 32832 rows trained. The floor is now MEASURED: step the real optimizer through the real schedule on a row whose gradient is always zero, giving 0.0322 relative (analytic 0.0323 for embed_lr=0.1 at train.py:263 with embed_wd=0.001 at :265 -- note line 820's decay-to-zero is inside `if isinstance(opt, Muon)` and never reaches this group). Every row clears it by >=2.65x, so the verdict does not sit near the 1.5x admission line. The selftest now carries the fully-trained table as a regression and asserts the 10x-median floor still fails it.
THE GATE-AT-1.5 INIT WORKS, which is what makes the flat result interpretable rather than a null launch: the arms track each other from the first logged step (step 10: 6.801 vs 6.798; step 100: 4.121 vs 4.110), so the VE arm is not spending its budget discovering a table hidden behind a zero gate.
decision: NOT ADOPTED. +16.3% parameters for -0.0001 nat is the whole case against it, and no seeds will be spent widening the bar for a change that is not being adopted -- the same call as A/B (3). Asymmetric summary, on purpose: there is NO evidence VE helps at 200M/0.26B, and the one non-flat reading (minimal_pairs -1.08pt) points the wrong way while staying inside its own bar, so 'harmless' is also unproven. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE: the hypothesis was never separated from capacity -- no equal-parameter control arm ran -- so a flat result cannot distinguish 'the mechanism does nothing' from 'the mechanism helps and the +16.3% of parameters spent on a gather hurts by the same amount'. It also does not transfer up: value embeddings are a nanogpt-speedrun result at a different scale and token budget, and a table fully trained at 0.26B may behave differently once the vocab is seen far more or far less often. To revisit, the cheap next step is the equal-parameter control (spend the 33.7M on width or depth instead), not another VE seed.

name: ab_untie_head
cmd: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,4,5,6 SKIP_BASE=1 ARM=untiehead STEPS=500 scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh  # then ARM=untieheadlr, same lane
notes: base reused: ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt (world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42). Launcher gained untiehead/untieheadlr arms and SKIP_BASE at 8692549b.
hypothesis:
b0-17: is the LM head's lr the mechanism behind the uniform embedding growth? THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, because one difference cannot separate the two candidate explanations -- this is the confound A/B (4) could not close and 1e's ruling fixes it here (2026-09-03):
  arm 1  base (REUSED ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt)  tied head, trains at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 2  --untie_head                            own head weights, STILL at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 3  --untie_head --head_lr 0.003464         own weights AND its own AdamW group
base->arm2 isolates CAPACITY (+33,619,968 params = +16.3%, 206,128,200 -> 239,748,168; the SAME magnitude as A/B (4)'s value_embed table, because both add one padded_vocab x d tensor). arm2->arm3 isolates the LR MECHANISM at IDENTICAL parameter count. WHY THE LR IS THE SUSPECT: train.py routes any parameter whose name contains tok or head into the embed group, so today's tied head necessarily trains at 0.1 -- 28.9x the nanochat reference head lr 0.004*(d/768)^-0.5 = 0.003464 at d1024 -- and b0-10 measured tok.weight growing 1.43x per 500 steps with 7.9% effective same-direction rate.
READING (pre-registered): domain_loss unweighted mean against 0.24 nat (ds.seed_variance_0p2b), minimal_pairs against 11.5pt (be.minimal_pairs_seed_variance), and tok.weight growth per 500 steps against b0-10's 1.43x. Verdict written as TWO differences, never one: a flat base->arm2 with a moving arm2->arm3 means the lr matters and the capacity does not; both flat means neither is readable at this scale and the +16.3% is unpaid-for; base->arm2 moving alone means this is a capacity result wearing an lr costume.
BASE IS REUSED, matched on the four things that decide comparability: world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42. Its cfg carries NO untie_head/head_lr field, which is the default (False, 0.0) -- absence here is not drift. Tokens/step therefore match, unlike the (3)/(2a) pair where world 5 vs world 4 made the same step a different token position and inverted the sign.
GUARD: scripts/test_untie_head.py, four checks each verified red on its own broken world. The one that matters most is that arms 2 and 3 are indistinguishable in every log except one lr field, so arm 3 collapsing into arm 2 errors nowhere and prints one number for two experiments; head lr is read by TENSOR IDENTITY, not group name, because a missing group returns None and would pass as a match. Also pinned: untying zeroes tok's vocab pad rows (while tied, one zero_() covered both tensors, so untied they would train in one arm only -- 1e caught this before the run), and the head stays fp8-excluded by name.

result: THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, and both differences are 9/9 same-sign but under the 0.24 nat bar. domain_loss unweighted_mean: base 2.8480 -> arm2 (untied@embed 0.1, +33,619,968 params = +16.3%) 2.8962 -> arm3 (untied@own 0.003464, IDENTICAL param count to arm2) 2.9139. base->arm2 +0.0482 nat (20% of the bar), 9/9 domains worse, sd 0.0342, t +4.23. arm2->arm3 +0.0176 (7% of the bar), 9/9 worse, sd 0.0116, t +4.55. base->arm3 +0.0659 (27%), 9/9, t +5.38. Per-domain a2-base spans +0.0078 (en_c4) to +0.0977 (zh_web), 12.5x; relative spans +0.221% to +3.403%, 15.4x, and the two orderings DISAGREE (zh_web is 1st absolute, 4th relative), so the domain structure is NOT a shadow of loss magnitude -- corr(base loss, absolute delta) = +0.592. minimal_pairs NOT READABLE by construction: the five 500-step A/B checkpoints all sit inside 4.33pt (sd 1.67pt) against an 11.5pt bar, so this metric cannot resolve any arm at this budget. val loss 2.603 -> 2.647 -> 2.668; train 2.332 -> 2.378 -> 2.383.

Removing the path must then reduce the growth. It INCREASES it: tok row-norm median 16.9115 -> 18.3308 (arm2, x1.0839) -> 19.8036 (arm3, x1.1710), and the LOWER the head's lr the MORE tok grows. The 11 alignment-padding rows [32773,32784) settle it, because they are never an input id and never a target, so they are reachable ONLY through the head and their movement IS that path rather than a proxy: arm2 and arm3 both read EXACTLY 0.0000 there (path completely removed, not weakened), while arm2's HEAD pad rows read 7.1036 against the tied base's 6.6575 (the path itself got 1.067x STRONGER). Named path fully removed, not weakened, effect moved the other way. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A GUESS, labelled: a tied table receives input-path and head-path gradients that partially cancel, and untying removes the cancellation so the input path alone pushes tok further; no gradient signs were measured, so only 'the head path inflates tok' is excluded. ARM 3 DOES NOT MEASURE THE LR MECHANISM AT STEADY STATE: its head reaches row-norm median 1.5375 = 2.4x the 0.64 init, i.e. barely trained, because 500 steps at 28.9x lower lr is not enough. Arm 2's head DID converge -- 16.4952 against the tied table's 16.9115, within 2.4% -- so arm 2's +0.0482 is not an initialization debt, while arm 3's extra +0.0176 largely is. CAPACITY IS NOT FREE AND NOT PAID FOR: +16.3% params makes every one of nine domains worse.
decision: NOT ADOPTED, and untie_head stays default False. Three consequences. (1) b0-10's uniform embedding growth needs a different mechanism: the head-path explanation is excluded by measurement, and the cancellation guess is the next thing to test -- it needs gradient signs on the two paths, not another A/B. (2) A/B (4) and b0-17 now agree on a pattern worth stating once: at 200M/500 steps, BOTH ways of spending +33.6M params on a padded_vocab x d table (value_embed, untied head) come in flat-to-worse. That is two independent arms of the same shape, which is a stronger statement than either alone. (3) The copy-init arm (untied head initialized FROM the embedding table) is now worth opening, and its purpose changed: not to control for the initialization confound (arm 2's head converged, so that confound is bounded) but as the only arm that can separate the tok reverse-growth from initialization cost at all. minimal_pairs should be dropped from 500-step A/B readings at 200M: 4.33pt of spread against an 11.5pt bar is not a measurement.

name: ab_untie_head
cmd: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,4,5,6 SKIP_BASE=1 ARM=untiehead STEPS=500 scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh  # then ARM=untieheadlr, same lane
notes: base reused: ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt (world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42). Launcher gained untiehead/untieheadlr arms and SKIP_BASE at 8692549b.
hypothesis:
b0-17: is the LM head's lr the mechanism behind the uniform embedding growth? THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, because one difference cannot separate the two candidate explanations -- this is the confound A/B (4) could not close and 1e's ruling fixes it here (2026-09-03):
  arm 1  base (REUSED ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt)  tied head, trains at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 2  --untie_head                            own head weights, STILL at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 3  --untie_head --head_lr 0.003464         own weights AND its own AdamW group
base->arm2 isolates CAPACITY (+33,619,968 params = +16.3%, 206,128,200 -> 239,748,168; the SAME magnitude as A/B (4)'s value_embed table, because both add one padded_vocab x d tensor). arm2->arm3 isolates the LR MECHANISM at IDENTICAL parameter count. WHY THE LR IS THE SUSPECT: train.py routes any parameter whose name contains tok or head into the embed group, so today's tied head necessarily trains at 0.1 -- 28.9x the nanochat reference head lr 0.004*(d/768)^-0.5 = 0.003464 at d1024 -- and b0-10 measured tok.weight growing 1.43x per 500 steps with 7.9% effective same-direction rate.
READING (pre-registered): domain_loss unweighted mean against 0.24 nat (ds.seed_variance_0p2b), minimal_pairs against 11.5pt (be.minimal_pairs_seed_variance), and tok.weight growth per 500 steps against b0-10's 1.43x. Verdict written as TWO differences, never one: a flat base->arm2 with a moving arm2->arm3 means the lr matters and the capacity does not; both flat means neither is readable at this scale and the +16.3% is unpaid-for; base->arm2 moving alone means this is a capacity result wearing an lr costume.
BASE IS REUSED, matched on the four things that decide comparability: world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42. Its cfg carries NO untie_head/head_lr field, which is the default (False, 0.0) -- absence here is not drift. Tokens/step therefore match, unlike the (3)/(2a) pair where world 5 vs world 4 made the same step a different token position and inverted the sign.
GUARD: scripts/test_untie_head.py, four checks each verified red on its own broken world. The one that matters most is that arms 2 and 3 are indistinguishable in every log except one lr field, so arm 3 collapsing into arm 2 errors nowhere and prints one number for two experiments; head lr is read by TENSOR IDENTITY, not group name, because a missing group returns None and would pass as a match. Also pinned: untying zeroes tok's vocab pad rows (while tied, one zero_() covered both tensors, so untied they would train in one arm only -- 1e caught this before the run), and the head stays fp8-excluded by name.
result: THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, and both differences are 9/9 same-sign but under the 0.24 nat bar. domain_loss unweighted_mean: base 2.8480 -> arm2 (untied@embed 0.1, +33,619,968 params = +16.3%) 2.8962 -> arm3 (untied@own 0.003464, IDENTICAL param count to arm2) 2.9139. base->arm2 +0.0482 nat (20% of the bar), 9/9 domains worse, sd 0.0342, t +4.23. arm2->arm3 +0.0176 (7% of the bar), 9/9 worse, sd 0.0116, t +4.55. base->arm3 +0.0659 (27%), 9/9, t +5.38. Per-domain a2-base spans +0.0078 (en_c4) to +0.0977 (zh_web), 12.5x; relative spans +0.221% to +3.403%, 15.4x, and the two orderings DISAGREE (zh_web is 1st absolute, 4th relative), so the domain structure is NOT a shadow of loss magnitude -- corr(base loss, absolute delta) = +0.592. minimal_pairs NOT READABLE by construction: the five 500-step A/B checkpoints all sit inside 4.33pt (sd 1.67pt) against an 11.5pt bar, so this metric cannot resolve any arm at this budget. val loss 2.603 -> 2.647 -> 2.668; train 2.332 -> 2.378 -> 2.383.
finding: THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, NOT UNSUPPORTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS IN THE WEIGHTS NOT THE LOSS. 1e's mechanism was that the TIED head trains tok.weight at embed_lr 0.1 through a second gradient path, which would make tok's uniform growth (b0-10) an artifact of that path. Removing the path must then reduce the growth. It INCREASES it: tok row-norm median 16.9115 -> 18.3308 (arm2, x1.0839) -> 19.8036 (arm3, x1.1710), and the LOWER the head's lr the MORE tok grows. The 11 alignment-padding rows [32773,32784) settle it, because they are never an input id and never a target, so they are reachable ONLY through the head and their movement IS that path rather than a proxy: arm2 and arm3 both read EXACTLY 0.0000 there (path completely removed, not weakened), while arm2's HEAD pad rows read 7.1036 against the tied base's 6.6575 (the path itself got 1.067x STRONGER). Named path fully removed, not weakened, effect moved the other way. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A GUESS, labelled: a tied table receives input-path and head-path gradients that partially cancel, and untying removes the cancellation so the input path alone pushes tok further; no gradient signs were measured, so only 'the head path inflates tok' is excluded. ARM 3 DOES NOT MEASURE THE LR MECHANISM AT STEADY STATE: its head reaches row-norm median 1.5375 = 2.4x the 0.64 init, i.e. barely trained, because 500 steps at 28.9x lower lr is not enough. Arm 2's head DID converge -- 16.4952 against the tied table's 16.9115, within 2.4% -- so arm 2's +0.0482 is not an initialization debt, while arm 3's extra +0.0176 largely is. CAPACITY IS NOT FREE AND NOT PAID FOR: +16.3% params makes every one of nine domains worse.
decision: NOT ADOPTED, and untie_head stays default False. Three consequences. (1) b0-10's uniform embedding growth needs a different mechanism: the head-path explanation is excluded by measurement, and the cancellation guess is the next thing to test -- it needs gradient signs on the two paths, not another A/B. (2) A/B (4) and b0-17 agree ONLY on the negative, and I overstated this before checking it: both spend +33,619,968 params (+16.3%) on one padded_vocab x d table and NEITHER pays for itself, but they are NOT the same result. value_embed is genuine noise -- per-domain delta 3/9 positive, mean -0.0002 nat, t -0.05, i.e. indistinguishable from zero in both sign and magnitude. The untied head is CONSISTENTLY WORSE -- 9/9 positive, mean +0.0482, t +4.23. So the shared claim is narrow: at 200M/500 steps neither use of that parameter budget helps. Calling them 'two independent arms of the same shape' would have claimed a reproduced effect where one arm has no effect at all, and the aggregate 'flat-to-worse' phrasing hides exactly that difference. (3) The copy-init arm (untied head initialized FROM the embedding table) is now worth opening, and its purpose changed: not to control for the initialization confound (arm 2's head converged, so that confound is bounded) but as the only arm that can separate the tok reverse-growth from initialization cost at all. minimal_pairs should be dropped from 500-step A/B readings at 200M: 4.33pt of spread against an 11.5pt bar is not a measurement.

hypothesis: N7: does running middle blocks twice buy depth at inference? RULED SEMANTICS (6e, option 3, pre-registered before any number): under AttnRes the second visit ADDS INTO the source the first visit wrote, so the ledger length is unchanged and final_ar still sees 25. Two premises of the ruling's wording are false on this checkpoint and the wrapper implements the semantics, not the wording -- attn_res_blocks=0 makes ar_block_ends {1..24} so 'partial' is always [] at the ar() read and the live accumulator is the done entry; and AttnRes has no per-source weight (g:(d,), q:(d,) only), so option 1 is the wrong experiment because it changes the depth-attention DISTRIBUTION, not because a weight vector runs out. KDA state rule (a) is the DEFINITION on this path, never '(a) beat (b)': model.py:125 passes no initial_state and discards the returned state, and the scoring path is one teacher-forced forward with no KV slots, so each visit starts from zero state by absence of plumbing. READING: humaneval gold BPB byte-weighted with paired per-task SE, domain_loss unweighted_mean with head_fp asserted equal, ms/token. Each arm must be scored in the topology it was TRAINED in; scoring loop-trained weights unlooped measures a weights-topology mismatch, not the loop.

result: NOT ADOPTED. 2x2 humaneval BPB byte-weighted (164 tasks / 29,662 bytes every cell): U-trained/U-scored 0.4635, U/L 0.4899, L/U 0.4828, L/L 0.4658. domain_loss unweighted_mean, head_fp identical on all 9 domains: 1.9858 / 2.1177 / 2.0810 / 1.9951. DIAGONAL (each arm in the topology it was trained in) U-U -> L-L: +0.0023 bits/byte, paired SE 0.0006, z +3.6, 103/164 tasks worse; +0.0093 nat, 9/9 domains worse, per-domain range +0.0054 to +0.0191. ms/token seq 1024 batch 1, 60 iters: looped/unlooped 1.336/1.284/1.329 on the SFT ckpt (mean 1.317, sd 0.028) and 1.223 on the data-leg ckpt, all four in [1.223, 1.336]. Training loss 250/250 identical to 0.001 (1.334 vs 1.335). unlooped path reproduces model._body BITWISE (max|diff| 0.000e+00) on every run
finding: THE MISMATCH IS THE FINDING, NOT THE LOOP. The two off-diagonal cells are 8-11x the diagonal and point in OPPOSITE directions: loop-trained weights run without the loop +0.0193 (z +8.4), normal weights run with the loop +0.0264 (z +11.3). So the cost at this scale is that weights and topology must MATCH, and either mismatch costs an order of magnitude more than the loop itself. This retro-explains Stage A: its +0.0273 is the mismatch-B cell (+0.0264), so Stage A measured the mismatch and never measured the loop -- and my first Stage B report repeated the error by scoring both arms unlooped, which controls the evaluation while breaking the variable that matters (6e caught it; 88% of the penalty I reported was my own design). Fairly scored the loop is slightly WORSE on both rulers and costs ~1.3x forward compute. Training loss being identical while both held-out rulers move against it means this is not 'the looped arm trained worse' but 'trained equally well, generalizes worse'; the 20-step probe's 1.375-vs-1.471 gap closed completely by step 250 and must not be quoted as an effect

Two numbers I published are RETRACTED: the 1.64x latency (one 20-iter run; the same checkpoint at 60 iters reads 1.223 and 1.640 is outside the range of all four reps, so ~1.3x is the figure) and 'training under the loop recovers 28% of the penalty' (there was no +0.0193 penalty to recover). BOUNDARY: 250 SFT steps on a 206M checkpoint rules out CHEAP adoption, not SMELT's from-scratch-under-the-loop claim, which we did not run. (2) the SHAPE-MATCHED rerun (one task, one row, one document, cu/aux hand-built as humaneval_bpb.py does versus doc_cu_seqlens/doc_prompt_lengths as sft_math.py does) agreed at max|dlogit| 0.4833 prefix / 0.3106 causal with aux ALL MATCH -- but 0.5 was MY threshold and a max logit difference is not a bound on BPB. THE NUMBER THAT SETTLES IT is the same quantity the row is written in: gold BPB computed from both constructions on those six tasks reads 0.3800 eval versus 0.3804 training, a difference of +0.0004 over 1119 solution bytes. That is 56x smaller than the +0.0228 under test, so the construction cannot account for the delta. ALSO REFUTED ON THE WAY, the leading hypothesis for a wiring bug: doc_prompt_lengths returned [117, 131, 83, 118, 123, 92] and the eval site's len(prompt) for the same tasks is identical, so the two sites do not derive different prompt lengths. SO THE ORIGINAL FINDING IS RESTORED: the matched cell fails the pre-registered rule in the wrong direction (+0.0228, 13.7 SE, 151/164 items worse, the count agreeing so it is not a few large items), while the SAME weights scored causally read 0.4612, better than the twin by 0.0031 at z +5.5 with 38/164 worse. Prefix training did not damage the weights; applying the bidirectional prompt mask at inference costs 0.0228, about 7.4x the weight-time gain. WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is not small: eval scores ONE document per row and training packs ~250, and the invalid run measured that packing alone moves these logits by 3-4 regardless of mask. So this arm's numbers are internally consistent -- every cell scored one-per-row -- but the regime the model TRAINED in was never scored, and 6e's original suspicion that a shape difference sits between the two sites is correct in substance even though it does not explain the 0.0228. The prompt-length binning refutation stands: the penalty is flat across quartiles (+0.0350 / +0.0287 / +0.0346 / +0.0296, 37-39 of 41 worse in every bin).
decision: NOT ADOPTED, as originally ruled, now on a verified number. The weights-only gain (-0.0031, z +5.5) is real but small, is collected by training with prefix and scoring causally, and is NOT recommended on one 500-step run at n=1 seed with seed sigma unmeasured -- 0.0031 is inside the range a seed could move. Recorded as a directional finding, not a recipe. Durable outputs: eff.flash_attn_cute_mask_mod_backward_wrong_sm90 and its two-call workaround; and the packing measurement above, which says a single-document eval is a different regime from a packed training batch by 3-4 logits and is worth its own fact if anything else in this repo compares the two.

name: n7c_p7_prefix7
cmd: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python3 sft_math.py --resume ckpt_data_leg_206m_8b.pt --sft_path data/sft/control_sft_ours.pt --out ckpt_n7c_p7.pt --max_steps 500 --batch 16 --save_every 250 --prefix p7 --loop 4 7
notes: Layer 7 works where layer 11 cannot because it has KDA layers above it to carry a prompt-position change into a supervised position; layer 11 is the last block and measured bitwise-identical. 6e had ruled layer 7 out as confounded with the loop, then lifted that when both arms turned out to be looped. Smoke test found a real defect: --loop enables grad_ckpt and forward HOOKS do not fire during a checkpoint recompute, so the recomputed layer 7 ran unmasked and torch raised CheckpointError on mismatched activation metadata. --loop alone and --prefix p3 alone both pass; only both together fail. Fixed by wrapping the target's forward (part of what the checkpoint recomputes) instead of hooking it, 63312c75. Smoke-tested 3 steps after the fix: 131/176 tensors differ from the loop-only run.
hypothesis: Prefix-LM on MLA layer 7 ALONE, inside the looped block, beats its causal twin ckpt_n7c_looped.pt on HumanEval gold BPB. This is the closest well-defined form of the original one-layer proposal. THE LOOP IS HELD CONSTANT: both this arm and its twin are looped 4-7, so prefix and loop are not confounded -- only the mask differs. Twin is an existing 500-step run at the same pack/seed/steps. READING RULE, pre-registered: adopt only if the paired delta is negative (better) by more than 2x its paired SE on the 164-task intersection AND the per-item count favours prefix; a delta inside 2 SE is a null. Scored in its own topology (looped 4-7) plus the causal-scored mismatch cell. Gate-certified on card 4 (pod ab92954d): A/A2/B/B2/C/D/E/F all pass for layer set [7]; the gate's real-length loss read -2.16e-04 vs causal, which is the effect under test and NOT a leak -- leakage is decided on the mask by exact enumeration (292919 newly visible pairs, 0 with a supervised key, 0 with a query outside the prompt).
result: HumanEval gold BPB, 164 tasks / 29662 bytes asserted per cell, all cells scored looped 4-7 as the arm trained. twin causal 0.4676 | arm+prefix 0.4673 (delta -0.0003, paired SE 0.0003, z +1.1, 73/164 items worse) | arm+causal 0.4666 (delta -0.0010, SE 0.0002, z +4.0, 67/164 worse). Final training loss 1.057, identical to the twin's 1.057; 19s/10 steps for both.
finding: THE PROVISIONAL FLAG IS LIFTED; the null stands. The eval path both arms were scored through is cleared by the same measurement that cleared P3's: with the shape held fixed the eval and training constructions produce gold BPB within +0.0004 of each other (0.3800 vs 0.3804 over 1119 solution bytes), 56x below the effect P3 turned on and far below anything that could move a -0.0003 delta. The arm reads -0.0003 against SE 0.0003, inside 2 SE, with 73/164 items worse, indistinguishable from chance. The training curve tracked its causal twin exactly (1.057 vs 1.057). Same scope caveat as P3: every cell was scored one document per row, and the packed regime the model trained in was not scored.
decision: NOT ADOPTED. Prefix-LM at MLA layer 7 alone under the 4-7 loop is a null on HumanEval gold BPB at 500 steps, n=1 seed. No re-score needed: the construction check that cleared P3 covers this arm's eval path too.

No custom insertion code: attn_every=4 at L=16 gives MLA at 3,7,11,15, identical to the looped arm's effective sequence with blocks 4..7 replayed, verified by constructing both instances and listing mixer kinds. Recipe otherwise identical to Stage D, seed 42, 3815 steps = 1.00008B tokens; warmup 300 absolute, warmdown 0.1 and anneal_frac 0 as fractions of total. Pre-registered reading in b0-25 before launch: 16L minus looped below -0.010 nat = new parameters beat repetition; within +-0.005 = repetition is as good, which the user's hypothesis predicts; above +0.005 = repetition BEATS new parameters, reported as its own case.
result: doc_cu unweighted_mean 2.3101 (val, 9 domains, 262144 tok/domain, wall 132.9s). Three-way on the SAME path (all three cu_path=doc_cu, runs/score_matrix.jsonl): equalcompute 2.2126, n8_fixed 2.2545, 16L-new 2.3101.
finding: The 16-layer new-parameter arm is the WORST of the three, +0.0975 nat behind equalcompute and +0.0556 behind n8_fixed, while carrying 154.6653M dedup parameters against the 12L arms' 122.3033M (+26.46%). So at 1B tokens on this mix, spending 26% more parameters on unique depth bought a loss that is worse, not better. It does not establish that depth is useless: 1B tokens is a short budget and a larger model is disadvantaged early, so this is one point on one budget and not a slope.
decision: Do not carry 16 unique layers into the head-hybrid A/B or the next scale point. It is also the nearest available reference for what a parameter increase buys at this scale, and its direction is NEGATIVE (+26.46% params -> +0.031 nat worse on the earlier reading, +0.0975 against the best arm here), which is why prereg b0_head_hybrid_3to1 says a B advantage below what +1.18% params buys is undecidable rather than assuming params help.

hypothesis: M3 at ONE pooled layer (1195^2 = 1,428,025 values, 1.46B memory params, layer 6) against M1's 1,048,576 and the control: readout 3's slope of block-paired doc_cu val against memory size, at equal dense params (206,128,200 all three), with the fp32 table master
result: stopped at step 652 by the controller under readout 4, alongside M1 (4c 2026-09-05). Last diag step 600: pool_touched_frac 0.0700 (stop below 0.20), topk_entropy 0.695, key_gini 0.9380 -- already past the threshold and on the same trajectory as M1, only steeper. Throughput ratio to the control was above the gate at every matched step: step 30 72937/82300 = 0.886, step 100 73165/82300 = 0.889 (4c predicted ~0.89). Readout 6 healthy: rows_changed_since_prev 1.09-1.25 at every window. Checkpoint: ckpt_b0_mem_m3.pt.interrupt.step652.
finding: Same key-usage collapse as M1 and faster at the larger table: 1,428,025 values reached 0.070 touched by step 600 where M1 at 1,048,576 was at 0.095 by step 1000. The larger the pool, the smaller the fraction the collapsed selection distribution covers, which is the direction a selection-side defect predicts and the opposite of what a value-update defect would give.
decision: Stopped before its own step 1000 because the fix is a design change that relaunches every arm for readout 3, so the remaining card time bought nothing. Not a null on readout 3: the size slope has no valid points at all.

name: b0_mem_m2
notes: launcher: harness launch --gate-timeout 793 --training; gate 155 GiB of cache / 0.39 GiB/s x2 -> 793s
hypothesis: M2 at ONE pooled layer (512^2 = 262,144 values, 0.27B memory params, layer 6) against M1's 1,048,576 and M3's 1,428,025: readout 3's slope of block-paired doc_cu val against memory size, at equal dense params (206,128,200 all arms), with the fp32 table master
finding: monitor: process exited 1
decision: check the log
retracted_reason: The verdict does not stand: status fail, result exit 1, finding monitor: process exited 1. The run did not crash. It was stopped by the controller at step 36 under readout 4 alongside M1 and M3 (4c 2026-09-05), by SIGTERM to both rank pids at 23:11:42Z; train.py:2786 _save_on_interrupt saved ckpt_b0_mem_m2.pt.interrupt.step36 (2,584,735,913 bytes, 23:11) and then raised KeyboardInterrupt(signal 15), which torchrun reports as ChildFailedError and the wrapper records as exit 1. The monitor cannot distinguish a controller kill from a crash by the exit code, so it wrote fail. WHAT THE RUN MEASURED, which the fail row does not carry: three diag rows at the non-uniform early windows -- step 10 pool_touched_frac 0.9423 entropy 3.425 gini 0.3906; step 20 0.6733 / 2.7375 / 0.7153, rows_changed 188438 ratio 1.068; step 30 0.3471 / 2.000 / 0.7632, rows_changed 105610 ratio 1.161. Throughput 75634 tok/s/gpu at step 30 = 0.919 of the controls 82300, above the 0.85 gate. Entropy falling and gini rising in 30 steps is the same direction as M1 and M3; the absolute fractions are not comparable across arms because the pool sizes differ and windows 1-10/11-20/21-30 are not the uniform 100-step windows readout 4 reads. M2 reached no step-1000 row, so it contributes no readout-4 verdict of its own.

hypothesis: MEASURES ONE DESIGN NUMBER, not a result about the arms. Pairing tightens the SE of a between-arm loss difference by sqrt(2)/sqrt(2(1-corr)), so corr decides whether the paired-BPB estimator earns its complexity: at corr 0.95 pairing is worth 4.5x the eval set, at corr 0.5 it is worth 1.4x and is not. Prediction before the run: corr > 0.9, because the two arms differ only in head mixing and easy tokens are easy for both -- but the b0 arms val losses differ by 0.015-0.097 nat against a per-token SD of ~1 nat, which is consistent with high corr and is NOT a measurement of it. Reported with the DOCUMENT-CLUSTERED SE beside the naive one: tokens within a document are not independent, so the naive SE understates by sqrt(deff), and a design decision reads the clustered number. 64 val rows = 262144 tokens over ~64 documents.

result: NO CORRELATION NUMBER. Two independent failures. (1) The job died on the GPU after both checkpoints loaded (card 7 peaked 3061 MiB): torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: misaligned address, raised inside fla/Tritons AUTOTUNER while benchmarking kernel configs for its disk cache (triton/runtime/autotuner.py:202 check_disk_cache -> bench_fn -> triton/testing.py:150 do_bench -> synchronize), not in the forward proper. (2) SEPARATELY, my claim never acquired: JOB=$$ inside a script launched as `setsid bash script.sh &` is the LAUNCHER shells pid, which exits at once, so card_claim was handed a zombie 60 times -- "pid 994178 holds no GPU device fd: [bash] <defunct>" -- and the job ran UNCLAIMED for its whole life. finding: The claim refusal is correct and names the incident it exists for (b0_mem_m1 2026-09-04, a claim on a process not on a card while the card reads ORPHAN). My error was reading "claim with the job pid, not $$" as "use $$ inside the job script": under setsid the script shell is not the process holding the device, the python child is. The right fix is to claim the PYTHON pid ($! after launching it), or to have the probe claim from inside after torch.cuda.set_device -- the only point that can know a device is really held. On the crash: it is in autotune rather than my arithmetic, and the untested candidate is shape -- batch 4 x seq 4096 at world 1 is a per-rank shape the arms never ran (they trained batch 16 accum 2 world 2), so the autotuner was benchmarking configs for a shape/arch combination with no cache entry. Not established.
decision: Do not spend another RL-team card on a debug cycle. Card-free work first: fix the claim to use the python pid plus a selftest world that fails a $$-under-setsid claim by asserting the claimed pid is the one holding the device; then try to reproduce the misaligned address with a minimal forward (one checkpoint, batch 1, 1 row) to separate shape from model. Only then ask for one more window with a written prediction. Fallback that needs no card at all: size the paired-BPB design for corr=0.8 (~8000 docs for SE(Delta)=0.0039 nat) with the assumption stated rather than measured.

name: e1_kda_shape_fault
finding: SHAPE REFUTED. All 5 cells PASS on card 5: b1/t128, b1/full-seq, b4/4096 which is the shape that crashed, b16/4096 which is the arms per-rank shape, and b4/chunk64. chunk_kda on random tensors at the crashing shape does not fault, so the per-rank shape alone does not reproduce the misaligned-address crash. The fault needs something this probe omits by design: loaded weights, a cold-vs-warm autotune cache, or the full model call sequence. This is NOT evidence the weights are bad -- the probe can only exonerate, and what it exonerated is the shape.
decision: Do not re-run arm_token_corr at batch 4 expecting a different outcome, and do not treat ckpt_b0_headmix_armA or armB as suspect on this evidence. The next discriminator is the autotune cache: re-run the failing arm_corr with TRITON_CACHE_DIR at an empty dir versus the warmed one, which separates cache state from weights without loading two checkpoints.

name: b0_moe_e1
notes: launcher: harness launch --gate-timeout 793 --training; cards 0,1,2,3,4,5,6; gate 155 GiB of cache / 0.39 GiB/s x2 -> 793s
hypothesis: E1 = 4x total capacity at EQUAL ACTIVE FLOPs and equal tokens, against the dense control ckpt_b0_headmix_armA (same launch line byte-for-byte plus the MoE flags, so scoring is block-paired on identical data order). THE NUMBER THIS RUN PRODUCES: (a) block-paired doc_cu val, arm minus control, at 1B tokens -- adopt at <= -0.010 nat, null at |delta| < 0.003; and (b) expert-load spread over 24 routed + 1 shared experts at w=768, from runs/moe_diag.jsonl every 100 steps. name: b0_e1p_dense
notes: launcher: harness launch --gate-timeout 793 --training; cards 1,2; gate 155 GiB of cache / 0.39 GiB/s x2 -> 793s
hypothesis: E1-PRIME ARM A (DENSE CONTROL), amendment 12, 3815 steps = 1.00B tokens, cards 1,2, world 2, --bf16. THE USER REVERSED THE READOUT-5 CLOSE: speed is a cost, not the value, so the MoE is judged on what 3.9x total params buys at 16% more time per token, not on the 16.2% structure cost. THE ADOPT RULE, pre-registered before this launch and not adjustable after: a MoE arm is adopted only if its val loss AT EQUAL WALL-CLOCK is below this arm's by more than 0.0444 nat, the sd of the LARGER of two four-seed families (facts/base_eval.json#be.one_seed_family_misstates_its_own_noise_by_2x: p02 seeds 0-3 = 3.7588/3.8085/3.7433/3.7009, sd 0.0444; the other family gives 0.0239 and that fact's own ruling is to use the larger, because understating noise ships a null as a finding). That number is measured at 0.2B tokens on mean domain loss, so it is an UPPER BOUND on seed noise here -- the rule can miss a small real gain, it cannot manufacture one. Between -0.0444 and +0.0444 is MEASURED, NOT ADOPTED. THIS ARM DEFINES EQUAL WALL-CLOCK: its total seconds to 1B tokens is the clock the MoE arms are read at, and the two val points bracketing that time will both be reported so the interpolation is visible. val every 200 steps. Paired with b0_e1p_moe24 (cards 3,4 pending their grant) which is the same line plus the six MoE flags. Readout 4's balance stop does not apply here (no experts). score_matrix at the end is REPORTED, not part of the adopt rule -- no threshold for it was pre-registered.

name: b0_cap_read_3ckpt
result: FLATTENS on the pre-registered criterion. cot's held-out slope over .step25000/25500/26000 is +0.00930/1k (se 0.00144) against +0.07290/1k (se 0.01345) over 22500/23000/23500 -- 0.13x, difference -0.06360 at 4.70 propagated se. Registered threshold was 'below half' (+0.03645), CONTINUES defined as within one propagated se; this is below the threshold and outside that band. Generalises to the other two dropped domains without being required to: chatml 0.30470->0.05310 (0.17x, 3.47 se), chat_qa 0.31260->0.06050 (0.19x, 3.07 se). The three unchanged-weight controls moved 0.73x (+0.01130 -> +0.00827/1k), flat within noise, so the decay is the dropped-domain component and not the instrument. head_fp 3160d1b11d04e9b8 for cot on all three checkpoints, matching amendment 5's recorded value, so both windows scored identical rows.
finding: SATURATING FORGETTING, NOT LINEAR, and the shape is the answer to the cap question rather than any single number. cot lost 0.1221 nats total (0.7512 at 22500 -> 0.8733 at 26000) at a rate now one eighth of its original. Amendment 10's warning that linear extrapolation gave an absurd +4.89 nats for chat_qa by step 38146 was right for the reason now measured: the rate was never linear, so no endpoint follows and a cap argued from the window-1 slope would have been argued from a transient. Three corroborations: aggregate share-weighted sum fell +0.02939 -> +0.00802/1k (0.27x); the pre-registered n=10 val refit at 24400 gave +0.01473/1k, between the two windows, where a span of 22600-24400 must land if the transient decays inside it; composition inverted, the dropped three carrying 78.1% of the rise then and 44.7% now, with zh_web (unchanged weight, at the drift floor) the largest single contributor at 20.1%. I ALSO REGISTERED THE WRONG EXPECTATION: amendment 10 said I expected UNRESOLVED at dof=1 per window, and the effect was large enough that three points sufficed. Recorded because a registration cited only when it was right is not doing its job.
decision: Registered as amendment 11 on runs/prereg.jsonl#moe48_30b_0907. Controller ruling (4c, 2026-09-07): the 4.0-epoch cap on cot/chatml/chat_qa STAYS for the rest of resume 1, and the cot-supply question moves to the resume 2 prereg. No stop. This row establishes that the two worlds are distinguishable and which one the data is in; it does not establish that 0.1221 nats of cot is an acceptable price for the epoch budget the ceiling fix bought, which is a judgement about the objective. Three things would overturn it, all in amendment 11: cot's slope rising again in a later window (a pause rather than a saturation -- two windows cannot show a rate STAYS low), the control floor moving while the dropped domains stay flat (attribution inverts), or any head_fp pair disagreeing between reads.

name: anneal_r_0909
notes: launcher: harness launch --gate-timeout 120 --training; cards 2,4,5,7
hypothesis: The anneal reweight arm. mix_200m_4b_annealR.json, --seed 1337 --sample_seed 42, identical to N1 in every other recipe value, so |R - N1| carries the reweight and nothing else. Read at the epoch-end val (val_batches_full=100) against the measured noise floor F = |N1 - N2| = |1.823 - 1.871| = 0.048. Criterion pre-registered at runs/prereg.jsonl#anneal_reweight_noise_floor_0908: if |R - N1| <= 0.048 the reweight has no measurable effect at 4B and is reported as a bound, not a failed run.
result: epoch-end val 1.819 (100 batches) vs N1 1.823; |R-N1| = 0.004, against F = 0.048 and D = 0.021
finding: NO EFFECT DETECTED, and the correct reading is a bound rather than a null. 0.004 is below both pre-registered floors by a factor of 5 and 12. But the design cannot resolve an effect of this size: N1's entire anneal tail moved val 1.854 -> 1.823 = 0.031, LESS than the 0.048 floor the reweight must clear, and D alone is 68% of that contribution. So this measures that the anneal reweight is not detectable at 4.00B tokens, not that it is absent. Two asymmetries in the reporting, both registered before the number existed (amendment 4): D is a max over 20-batch periodic reads while F is the 100-batch epoch-end read, so D carries extra sampling noise and is an upper bound on true drift -- it over-penalises R, which means this null carries a caveat that an effect verdict would not have; and no clean epoch-end D exists structurally, because the epoch-end R-vs-N1 comparison IS the verdict quantity once R's anneal differs. The ep-line train figure (R 1.601) is excluded from every comparison: it is one micro-batch, and the same null pair puts its spread at 0.410, 8.5x the val floor (facts/efficiency.json#eff.ep_line_train_is_one_microbatch).
decision: The anneal reweight does NOT enter the 30B mix on this evidence, and the reason recorded is the power limit rather than the bound. Any future test of an anneal-phase change at this budget is under-powered by construction and should either lengthen the anneal, raise the token budget, or read a metric whose floor is smaller than the phase's own contribution. The 13-read replicate-drift series (runs/anneal_r_vs_n1_drift_0909.tsv, D = 0.021) is reusable as the drift floor for any same-seed pair at this configuration.

name: csa_step_probe_0909
hypothesis: CSA step-speed probe for v2 launchability. Per-step wall time of GatedMLA with csa=True (m=4, csa_topk=512, n_win=128, the v2 spec's CSA-with-SWA from prereg v2_loop_moe_csa_0908) vs csa=False (latent MLA), same shape d=1024 heads=8, B=16 T=4096, bf16, packed cu path one doc per row, same card, forward+backward, alternating, median of 20 after 3 warmup; B falls back 16->4->1 on OOM and the fallback is reported. DECISION RULE, stated before the number exists: ratio = median(csa)/median(control). ratio <= 1.15 -> the v2 first arm is launchable on the reference implementation; ratio > 1.15 -> the arm needs a fast path before launch and the v2 schedule changes. Why 1.15: the arm's verdict is per-FLOP and the loop already multiplies FLOPs by 1.5, so a kernel penalty under 15% of the control step is smaller than the multiplier it would be confounded with, and ~0.6 extra wall-days on a ~4-day control arm is cheaper than writing a kernel first. The reference self-describes as O(T^2) in the select gather (model.py:242-244), so the tail risk is several-fold, not 15% -- the probe exists because the number is unknown. Result lands in facts/efficiency.json#csa with the config in the fact.
result: B=16 T=4096 D=1024 heads=8 bf16, packed cu (one doc per row), fwd+bwd, median of 20 after 3 warmup, same card (2), alternating: control GatedMLA csa=False 28.59 ms/step (2,292,376 tok/s); CSA m=4/topk=512/n_win=128 233.19 ms/step (281,041 tok/s); ratio csa/control = 8.157 (mean 233.19, min 233.07 -- no warmup drift). No OOM at B=16. Log runs/csa_step_probe_0909.log, instrument probes/csa_step_probe.py.
finding: The reference CSA implementation is 8.2x slower per step than the flash-varlen MLA path at the v2 config. The pre-registered decision rule (in this row's hypothesis) was 1.15x: the arm is launchable on the reference at or under it, and needs a fast path first above it. 8.157 is past it by a factor of seven, so the v2 first arm CANNOT be read on the reference even if it finishes -- its per-FLOP verdict would confound the loop's 1.5x with an 8.2x kernel penalty. The cost is where the docstring warned it was: the select branch materialises (B,H,T,topk*m) = (16,8,4096,2048) scores in PyTorch against MLA's flash kernel. The number is the reference's cost, not the architecture's: a fused select/window kernel is the fast path, and the arm's correctness case (test_arch_compat cases 1/4/4b) is unaffected by speed.
decision: v2 first arm does not launch until a CSA fast path exists (fused select+window kernel, or a topk/indexer that does not materialise the full T x selected score matrix). The v2 schedule changes: kernel work enters the critical path before the 30B arm. HCA and partial RoPE stay unbuilt per amendment_3 sequencing (4c confirmed 2026-09-09). Number lands in facts/efficiency.json#csa with the config, via PR with the instrument. Card 2 released; claim acquire timed out only because the job finished inside the 90s window -- no claim file was written, verified.

The 14-point gap between 0.00% and 14.0% is the PROMPT FORMAT, and the mechanism is measured rather than inferred: at the position HumanEval's prompt ends -- immediately after a function docstring -- P(<eos>) = 0.3131, second only to newline at 0.5014 (fb probe, ckpt .step34000, runs/probe3.log). Inside a started body P(<eos>) = 0.0000 and the model completes correctly: greedy produced a correct trial-division is_prime and a complete Stack class (push/pop/top/__len__/__repr__/__getitem__). So the model holds the algorithms and fails to ENTER the body from a docstring. Three demos supply that scaffolding; HumanEval by construction does not. This also predicts l1_fewshot's answer_present 0.340 -- 66% of math generations yielding no parseable answer is the same termination defect, not arithmetic failure.
decision: 0.00% is the number to quote externally; 14.0% is in-house and not comparable to anything published. Do not report the 3-shot figure as a HumanEval-like result. The cheap lever this exposes is termination, not capability: any SFT that teaches where a function body starts and ends should move HumanEval off the floor without more pretraining tokens. hypothesis: Format SFT on sig+docstring->body pairs (data/sft/sft_format_0909.pt: 98,873 examples packed into 6,714 rows x 4097 tok = 27.5M tok, prefix_mismatches 0, vocab_id 0bce3584bc24f255 matching the base) teaches the model to emit a function BODY at the position HumanEval hands over, instead of the next top-level construct. Base is ckpt_1.5b-a0.2b-e48_30b.milestone_keep_fb_step34000.pt, official-protocol HumanEval pass@1 0/164 with 160/164 empty (facts/base_eval.json#be.humaneval_pass1_step34000). The failure is positional, not semantic: 127/164 are cut at position 0 by a stop string (123 by newline-def), 33/164 argmax <eos>; four spaces of bare indentation drop mean P(<eos>) 0.2820 -> 0.0118 and lift pass@1 to 4/164, where the model wrote a body 99 times and was right 4 -- ~4% conditional capability. PREDICTION: post-SFT pass@1 under the OFFICIAL protocol lands near 4/164 = 2.4% with the empty rate collapsing from 160 to under 40. Prereg threshold >=5/164 (Fisher one-sided p=0.030 vs 0/164), runs/prereg.jsonl#format_sft_humaneval_0909. A post-SFT empty rate that stays high refutes the format explanation; a low empty rate with pass@1 still 0 says capability, not format, is binding. Reference frame: Phi-1 (1.3B dense, 7B tokens) reports 50.6% pass@1 off ~180M tokens of exercise-format synthetic data IN PRETRAINING; this pack is the same intervention at 27.5M tokens and post-hoc, so it tests the format claim, not the ceiling.
result: HumanEval pass@1 (greedy, official protocol) 3/164 = 1.83%, up from 0/164. Empty completions 72/164 = 43.9%, down from 160/164. Empty split: eos_first 70, stop_at_0 2 (base: stop_at_0 127, eos 33).
finding: The prereg threshold was NOT met: 3/164 against 0/164 is Fisher one-sided p=0.124, where >=5/164 was needed for p=0.030. The prediction was near 4/164 with the empty rate under 40; pass@1 landed close and the empty rate did not. Format is confirmed as a large effect, capability is not bought -- the split the prereg named. The sharper reading is in the empty SPLIT rather than the empty total: stop_at_0 collapsed 127 -> 2 while eos_first roughly doubled 33 -> 70. The SFT taught the model where a turn ends, and did not teach it what to put in the body. Reading 160 -> 72 alone would call this a partial success of one mechanism; the split says one mechanism was nearly eliminated and a second grew into its place.
decision: The capability question is answered and the flagship line is retired (user order, same day): 27.5M tokens of post-hoc format SFT moves format and not capability, against phi-1's 180M tokens of exercise-format data IN PRETRAINING for +21.6 points. p1 is a new model on a new corpus, docs/standards/p1_data_recipe.md. Closed by fb at 14:2xZ, ~2h after the measurement: the row that recorded it lived in a diverged worktree copy while this row, the one on main carrying the prereg hypothesis, stayed open.
